'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Sonny Perdue]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Nathan Deal]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsGA}} The '''2010 Georgia gubernatorial election''' was held on November 2, 2010. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Sonny Perdue]] was term-limited and unable to seek re-election. [[Partisan primary|Primary elections]] for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] parties took place on July 20. Democrats nominated former governor [[Roy Barnes]], and Republicans nominated Representative [[Nathan Deal]] following a [[Two-round system|runoff]] on August 10. The [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian Party]] also had [[ballot access]] and nominated [[John Monds]]. Deal won the general election, and took office on January 10, 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.ajc.com/news/georgia-politics-elections/georgia-election-deal-defeats-714575.html|title=Deal defeats Barnes to take Governor's Mansion |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=2010-09-03}} {{As of|2024}}, this was the last election in which a candidate won the governorship by double digits. This is the first gubernatorial election in Georgia since [[1990 Georgia gubernatorial election|1990]] in which the winner was of a different party than the incumbent president. This was the first election in which Republicans won three consecutive gubernatorial elections in the state. This was the last gubernatorial election in which [[Douglas County, Georgia|Douglas]], [[Henry County, Georgia|Henry]], and [[Newton County, Georgia|Newton]] counties voted for the Republican candidate and the last in which [[Baker County, Georgia|Baker]], [[Early County, Georgia|Early]], [[Mitchell County, Georgia|Mitchell]], [[Clinch County, Georgia|Clinch]], [[Brooks County, Georgia|Brooks]], and [[McIntosh County, Georgia|McIntosh]] counties voted for the Democratic candidate. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== *[[Jeff Chapman (politician)|Jeff Chapman]], [[Georgia Senate|State Senator]] *[[Nathan Deal]], [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]][http://www.wtoctv.com/global/story.asp?s=10286057]{{dead link|date=August 2010}} *[[Karen Handel]], [[Secretary of State of Georgia]] *[[Eric Johnson (Georgia politician)|Eric Johnson]], former state senator *Ray McBerry, candidate for governor in [[2006 Georgia gubernatorial election|2006]] *[[John Oxendine]], insurance commissioner *Otis Putnam ====Declined==== *[[Johnny Isakson]], incumbent U.S. senator{{Cite web|url = https://apnews.com/article/georgia-johnny-isakson-legislature-state-legislature-congress-89123ff83d37e40728b1005fe45224fa|title = Johnny Isakson, former Georgia Republican U.S. senator, dies|last = Amy|first = Jeff|date = December 19, 2021|website = Associated Press}} ===Polling=== ====Primary==== {| class="wikitable" |- valign=bottom ! style="width:150px;"| Poll source ! style="width:140px;"| Dates administered ! style="width:80px;"| John
